Actually boiling water to spin a turbine is a very common method. Nuclear power plants do just that. They use radioactive decay to heat the water, turning it into steam. Hydroelectric dams are unimaginably destructive to the local environment.

Using electricity from the wall can be derived using many different sources. Today, most electricity world-wide is produced at coal fired power-plants. Technically, the answer to your question lies in what mix of powerplants are supplying the grid in your area.

Another thing to throw in the mix is that transmission lines vary in their efficiency based on distance, voltage level, and a few other variables.
